title: Existence of exact perfect integral stratum charts with normalized pullback squares
statement: Fix l prime and E/Q_l finite. Let h:W→X be a morphism of Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with l invertible in global sections on both. For every integral constructible object K in the canonical adic presentation, there exists Charts(l,E,h,K), with all strata, covers, finite-projective models, exact restrictions, base-changed covering data and projection-normalized chart squares as defined in [def-a1-integral-stratum-chart-restrictions-data]. This is only the chart construction; it asserts no global scalar or triangulated compatibility for h.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to $T=X$, $A=R$ and $\varpi=\pi$. Its final category-identification clause identifies the category in the question with condition (i), and (i) implies (ii). Thus choose its finite stratification and, on each stratum, a pro-etale trivializing cover. The strata are constructible: on each member of a finite Noetherian affine cover of $X$, [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] gives a Noetherian underlying space, so by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] every open subset is quasi-compact, hence retrocompact, and a locally closed subset is an open intersected with the complement of an open; constructibility is local on this finite open cover. Choose for each perfect value a bounded finite-projective representative $P_{\alpha t}^\bullet$. The scalar extension in (ii), computed on that representative, is $B_{V_{\alpha t}}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{P_{\alpha t}^\bullet}$: the constant finite-projective terms are summands of finite free constant modules, hence flat (tensor with a finite free module is a finite direct sum). By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] this bounded-above constant complex is K-flat, so it computes the indicated derived scalar extension. This is exactly the requested chart isomorphism, with the completed coefficient restriction of (ii). The hypotheses needed by this characterization are precisely the assumed Noetherianity, finite dimension and invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$.

proof.text: For a stratum immersion $u$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] says its inverse image on module sheaves is exact and preserves all small limits. The canonical identification $u^{-1}B_T\cong B_S$ and the comparisons with finite reductions are those of [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison]; that lemma also says ordinary restriction of a derived-complete complex stays derived complete and its specified completion comparison is invertible. Combine this comparison with $\gamma_u$ from [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] to identify ordinary exact restriction with the specified integral pullback: the map from the latter to ordinary restriction is the inverse of the ordinary-to-completed comparison composed with $\gamma_u$. Both comparisons identify each finite quotient projection with the actual quotient map. The same lemma on immersions places the restricted object in the integral constructible category, with the same uniform interval for the reductions.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8 and Remark 6.5.10, pp.50-51; proetale.tex Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion

proof.text: For a chosen site-object arrow $v:V\to S$, [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies its actual inverse image, on rings and underlying abelian sheaves, with restriction to $S_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$. Module actions restrict under the same identification. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] this module restriction is exact and has a left adjoint, hence preserves small limits, including countable products. In particular it sends the coefficient limit to $B_V$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-stratum-completion-unit] with the original Noetherian scheme $X$, the chosen stratum and its object $V$: it gives compatibility with finite derived reductions and the completion unit, and preservation of completeness. By [lem-sp-slice-restriction-strict-derived-limit] the derived-limit comparison commutes with every projection. Consequently the restricted completion unit identifies ordinary restriction with completed pullback; composing with $\gamma_v$ of [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] identifies it with the specified integral pullback, including the finite projections. This argument needs no Noetherianity of $V$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8 and Remark 6.5.10; sites.tex Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero

proof.text: Here the derived-limit comparisons are comparisons of the actual strict models. If $F$ is any restriction just obtained and $C_\bullet$ a strict tower of complexes, its product comparison sends the $n$-th projection of $F(\prod C_n)$ to $F(C_n)$. For the transition endomorphism $s$ this gives $F(s)$ equal to the endomorphism defined by the restricted transitions, since both have $n$-th coordinate $F(t_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Applying [lem-pur-roos-additive-comparison] therefore identifies $F(\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1])$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_F)[-1]$, by the product comparison in both coordinates. It is natural in strict tower maps. Exactness of $F$ permits passage to the derived categories. Thus the comparisons in Steps 2-3 commute with the strict-tower Roos construction, with its finite projections and with the quotient transitions, rather than just identifying the endpoints of triangles.

proof.text: For $g=i_\alpha$ and $U=V_{\alpha t}$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-derived-restriction-comparisons] with $R$ there equal to $B_X$. Its cohomology comparison gives $v_{\alpha t}^{-1}i_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal H^j(K)\cong\mathcal H^j(v_{\alpha t}^{-1}i_\alpha^{-1}K)$. The coefficient identifications established above make these comparisons comparisons of modules over $B_{V_{\alpha t}}$. Composing with the chart isomorphism from Step 1 proves the asserted cohomology compatibility. If $\mathcal H^j(K)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, its exact restriction is zero, hence the displayed scalar complex has no cohomology in those degrees. This concerns the cohomology of the scalar model; no claim that its chosen finite-projective representative has terms only in $[a,b]$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, perfect-values convention; exact restriction cohomology calculation

proof.text: Apply [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] to $h$ and the chosen finite stratification. It gives the actual locally closed immersions $S'_\alpha=W\times_X S_\alpha\to W$, whose pairwise disjoint images are $h^{-1}|S_\alpha|$ and cover $W$. These subsets are constructible: on each member of a finite Noetherian affine cover of $W$, [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] gives a Noetherian topological space, so [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] makes every open subset quasi-compact; express a locally closed subset as a closed subset intersected with such an open. Constructibility is local on this finite open cover. Discard empty strata. For each remaining stratum base change the chosen covering family along $S'_\alpha\to S_\alpha$. The resulting arrows are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and form an fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], hence a pro-etale covering by the definition of the site. Its objects are exactly $V'_{\alpha t}=W\times_X V_{\alpha t}$.

source.place: Tag 022D, lemma-fpqc (3); weakly etale base change; finite constructible stratification pullback

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $Lh^*K$ is integral constructible and its canonical $n$-th reduction is $h^{-1}K_n$. Apply Steps 2-4 to $W$, $i'_\alpha$, and $v'_{\alpha t}$: $W$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, $i'_\alpha$ is a locally closed stratum immersion and $v'_{\alpha t}$ is an object of its pro-etale site. This proves all the primed exact-restriction, coefficient, product and Roos assertions. The same preservation lemma applied to $i_\alpha$ and to $v_{\alpha t}$, together with Steps 2-3, places $i_\alpha^{-1}K$ and $v_{\alpha t}^{-1}i_\alpha^{-1}K$ in their integral constructible categories. Thus the integral composition comparisons used next are applied only to objects in their stated domain, even when the chart schemes are not Noetherian.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(5), pp.50-51; Lemma 6.5.8 and localization for primed restrictions

proof.text: Write $q=i_\alpha\circ v_{\alpha t}:V_{\alpha t}\to X$ and $q'=i'_\alpha\circ v'_{\alpha t}:V'_{\alpha t}\to W$. The fibre-product square gives the equality $h\circ q'=q\circ g_{\alpha t}$. Use [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], whose convention is $c_{a,b}:L(b\circ a)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*Lb^*$, to form the following natural isomorphisms. First Steps 2-3 and $c_{v',i'}$ identify the requested left side with $Lq'^*Lh^*K$. Apply $c_{q',h}^{-1}$ to reach $L(h\circ q')^*K=L(q\circ g)^*K$; apply $c_{g,q}$ to reach $Lg^*Lq^*K$; finally apply $Lg^*(c_{v,i})$ and the exact-restriction identifications to reach $Lg^*(v^{-1}i^{-1}K)$. This defines the desired comparison and proves its invertibility. The same composition lemma specifies that its reduction is the canonical finite-coefficient composition comparison. Since the restriction identifications preserve their finite projections, reducing this displayed composite gives precisely the two finite-coefficient factorizations of $V'_{\alpha t}\to X$. Its naturality follows from naturality of each factor. Empty strata require no comparisons.
